title: Lipogram
rule: No letter e anywhere on the page, folio title included; the four lines are rewritten to fit.
made: six panels printed as HANDMADE stencils in five flat dyes plus a wall wash (indigo, madder, ochre, verdigris, umber, skin): one cut stencil per colour from the b1m2 cut model, paper ties (bridges) cut across every large opening, a fixed misregistration per colour, mottled dye with pooling at the stencil edges, on the LoC 1934 sheet
the ANRC 1922 key cutout used as a stencil, printed in ochre; the memo's 'key' drawn as a small umber key instead of written
captions and rewritten lines in the shared pen hand (all strings asserted e-free at build time); folio 'Lipogram 08' by pen99.folio

question.canon: Pardon me — have you the right time?
question.page: Pardon! Do you know what o'clock it is?

answer.canon: Ten past four, by the clock.

forgetting.canon: Well, here I am... and what for?
forgetting.page: So, I'm at my cupboard... and what for?

substitutions.memo: '4:15: unlock SRVC door. [drawn key] in cupboard.'

page_strings: Randolph, 1937. A railway man at his post finds a slip: unlock SRVC door at 4:15. Up, and off to his cupboard.
Halfway, a woman at his window calls out:
Our man looks up at a wall clock:
His visitor nods and walks off.
At his cupboard. Door flung back: a brass thing hangs on its hook, with a tag: SRVC.
Brass stays on its hook. SRVC door stays shut.

events.E0: P1: the memo slip on the desk, the agent rising to go
events.E1: P2: the stranger at the window, question
events.E4: P5: cupboard open, brass key on its hook, tag SRVC
events.E5: P6: pencil to chin, the forgetting line; key on its hook, SRVC door shut

beat: the page is printed stencil by stencil: wall wash, ochre, verdigris, indigo, madder and skin, umber; then the e-free lettering is laid
beat_frames: b05: + madder and skin (clock, her coat, faces)
b06: + umber (trousers, hair, hands of the clock)

self_check.check: No letter e (upper or lower case) appears anywhere, folio title included: every lettered string on the page is listed in page_strings and asserted e-free at build time (measured); the photographs and stencils carry no lettering
self_check.evidence: measured (strings) and perceptually judged (from frames) by the maker

weaknesses: '4:10' is written in figures to avoid 'ten'
the cupboard reads as an open frame more than a solid piece of furniture
